newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares rise in speculative trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares rise in speculative trade.

text.p: Speculation was to thank for a general increase in share prices in busy Thursday trade on the Nigerian stock exchange, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 6,841.43 from 6,819.15 on Wednesday.
Many blue chips were stronger on demand but a handful with large quantities of their shares on offer dropped back.
Resurgent brewing shares closed higher again but some traders said the rise was at too fast a pace.
Nigerian Breweries went 60 kobo higher at 17.00 naira and Guinness was 6.80 naira, up 10 kobo.
"The way Nigerian Breweries is moving is frightening; it may not be long before it starts to dip again," one trader told Reuters.

Oil shares were on the rise too. Agip touched 20.00 naira with a 25 kobo gain, Unipetrol hit 53.00 naira on a 40 kobo rise while Total at 54.80 naira, Texaco at 31.51 and Mobil at 46.50 naira all went 20 kobo up.
Investors continued to buy West African Portland Cement. It finished 60 kobo up at 42.20 naira. Ashaka and Benue Cement dropped 20 kobo and 10 kobo respectively to 18.10 naira and 7.70 naira.
Conglomerate UAC fell 41 kobo to 7.99 naira because investors were offloading large quantities. CFAO too lost 10 kobo to 3.20 naira for the same reason.
A.G. Leventis added one kobo at 1.60 naira on its improved third quarter result to end-September.

Three big banks fell. Union Bank dropped 15 kobo to 5.60 naira, Guaranty Trust Bank and NAL Merchant Bank were each 10 kobo weaker at 12.70 naira and 4.80 naira respectively. FSB International Bank finished five kobo higher at 5.50 naira.
